C-05.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category and should stand. Read against the two PDFs, the record describes no disagreement at all: it files a one-point gap (88% vs 87%) that its own resolution_note calls "within noise", and neither claim describes the paper it is attached to. P-85 (Pu et al., NeuroImage 310, 2025) feeds task-state prefrontal fNIRS phase-locking connectivity plus MMSE/BNT/HVLT scores and completion times (137 features, PCA-reduced) into nine default-parameter classical classifiers under five-fold CV on 203 Chinese recruits (48 NC/65 SCD/90 MCI); its headline is MCI vs NC accuracy 0.920, AUC 0.970 (LR, MMSE task). It has no attention component and no ADNI data. P-86 (Kim et al., NeuroImage 325, 2026) is a single 3-class AD/MCI/normal classifier on T1 MRI (3D CNN on volumes + modified GAT with self-attention on CIVET thickness, embeddings z-scored, projected, concatenated into a fully connected layer), 1,900 scans that are 88% NACC/8% ADNI/4% Hanyang, stratified five-fold CV; its MCI AUC is 0.719 (95% CI 0.691-0.747; 72.3% in the Results text). It uses no SVM and reports no 87% or 88% performance figure. Under the brief's ordering, outcome 1 applies before outcome 2 because the record's claims misread both papers and the record states no disagreement. I checked whether any other category fits better: not genuine, because the papers report different estimands (binary MCI vs NC accuracy/AUC on fNIRS+scales versus one-class AUC inside a 3-class structural-MRI task), neither claims an ordering the other refutes, three of four deterministic gates fail with no waiver, and P-85's AUC 0.970 from internal CV on 138 participants trips the performance-validity exclusion in any case. Not documented_incommensurability as filed, because that category presupposes a record that at least states two real results; the verdict is right that a corrected record with the papers' actual figures would land there. No third studies are needed, and the PDFs settle it, so partially_resolved and unresolved do not apply.
C-05.grounds_check: All nine grounds are supported by the PDFs; none is wrong. Verified in detail: (1) both PDFs carry the titles, authors and journal issues the pack map and record point to; (2) "attention" occurs in P-85 only as a cognitive domain (5 hits, e.g. p.2 "cognitive functions, including attention, executive function"), never as a model component, and the nine models are listed on p.5 and p.16; (3) P-85 participants were recruited from Kangci Hospital of Jiaxing, Shanghai Mental Health Center, factories, a school class, a convalescent home, communities and villages in Zhejiang and Shanghai (p.3), and "ADNI" does not appear anywhere in P-85; (4) no P-85 figure is attributed to an attention model, and the headline 92.0%/97.0% is on p.1 and p.16; (5) P-86 contains no "SVM" or "support vector" and its fusion is concatenation into a fully connected layer (p.5), while self-attention is P-86's GAT (p.3); (6) P-86 Table 1 gives Hanyang 76 (4%), ADNI 145 (8%), NACC 1679 (88%) on p.2, and the pack's registry row for P-86 does say Dataset "ADNI", ADNI_Dependent "true", Task_Type T1/MCI_vs_HC, so the verdict's remark that the registry is contradicted by Table 1 is accurate; (7) "87" appears in P-86 only inside reference page ranges and DOIs, and "88" only as the NACC share, Table 4 cells 88.2 and 88.8, and DOIs; (8) the record's resolution_note literally says "Marginal performance difference within noise"; (9) task, dataset-family and modality-family gates fail on the substance (three binary NC/SCD/MCI tasks vs one 3-class AD/MCI/normal task; own Chinese recruits vs NACC-dominated multi-site; fNIRS plus paper-and-pencil scales vs structural MRI) and only validation tier matches (both internal five-fold CV, V2). Two small precision notes, neither affecting the verdict: the verdict calls P-86's MCI AUC "one-vs-rest", a term P-86 never uses (it reports per-class ROC curves in Fig. 6 and per-class AUCs in the Results, which is the one-vs-rest construction, so the label is a fair inference but is presented as if the paper said it); and "macro-averaged per-class metrics" conflates P-86's statement that accuracy/precision/recall/F1 are macro-averaged (p.5) with its per-class Tables 3 and 4, an inconsistency that belongs to P-86 rather than the verdict. The performance-validity ground is correctly scoped: AUC 0.970 sits exactly at the >=0.97 threshold, from internal five-fold CV on 48 NC + 90 MCI with no external cohort, and the verdict rightly treats it as non-decisive because the contested "88%" is not that figure.

C-05.would_change: Nothing in these two PDFs. If the record is rewritten with the papers' actual figures (P-85 MCI vs NC accuracy 0.920 / AUC 0.970 from fNIRS plus scales, internal five-fold CV; P-86 MCI AUC 0.719 within a 3-class AD/MCI/normal structural-MRI task, stratified five-fold CV), the correct category becomes documented_incommensurability, with the task, dataset-family and modality-family gate failures and the metric-definition difference named on the record; it could not become genuine because P-85's headline AUC also meets the performance-validity exclusion.

C-235.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category, applied in the brief's order. The ledger record itself describes no disagreement on any quantity: its resolution reads "Both architectures are internally valid; the conflict marks an open modelling question, not an error in either paper", its apparent_performance_gap calls the two results "incommensurable by construction", and genuine_conflict is already false. That is the "architectural fork in which both findings are presented as true" example the brief lists under false_positive. Read against the PDFs, no same-quantity incompatibility exists: P-989 (Yoon et al. 2023) reports Cox HRs for aMCI-to-AD-dementia conversion by MBI cluster and by MBI domain in a Seoul memory-clinic cohort (n=1,184, mean 3.1 y); P-997 (Meng et al. 2023) reports per-symptom linear mixed-model slopes and GEE odds of PD-MCI in drug-naive PPMI PD patients (n=423, 5 y). Where the papers come nearest to touching, they point the same way: impulse-type symptoms (P-989 NPI-Q impulse dyscontrol HR 1.920 [1.444-2.554] vs P-997 QUIP ICDs OR 1.173 [0.830-1.659]; overlapping intervals, different constructs, HR vs OR) and depression (P-989 affective-dysregulation domain HR 1.373 [1.049-1.796] vs P-997 GDS-15 depression OR 2.575 [1.771-3.744]). Genuine is excluded. Documented_incommensurability would also describe the pair (population, outcome, metric type and dataset family all differ, no waiver on record), but the ordering rule puts false_positive first when the record describes no disagreement, and the verdict correctly names incommensurability as the fallback. One point the verdict does not discuss: P-989's affective-dysregulation-only cluster was not associated with AD progression (HR 1.214 [0.883-1.670], p=0.232; SGDS>6 subgroup HR 1.237 [0.850-1.798], p=0.266, p7) while P-997's depression OR for PD-MCI is 2.575 [1.771-3.744], and those two intervals do not overlap. This is the only place an adversarial reader could try to build a contradiction, but the record does not claim it, the direction is the same (both above 1), and the quantities differ on every axis the rule names (HR for time to AD dementia in aMCI vs OR for PD-MCI occurrence in PD; a depression/anxiety-only cluster vs any GDS-15>=5 depression regardless of co-occurring symptoms). It could at most be documented incommensurability, never genuine, so the verdict stands.
C-235.grounds_check: All six grounds are supported by the papers. (1) P-997 models each symptom separately: methods p3 "the presence/absence of NPS at baseline, visit, and visit*NPS interaction term" in each model; one table per symptom (Tables 1-5); no count, cluster or aggregation analysis anywhere in the paper. (2) P-989 Table 4 (p5) gives per-domain multivariable Cox HRs, all significant: MBI-positive 1.783, decreased motivation 2.131, affective dysregulation 1.373 (p=0.021), impulse dyscontrol 1.920, social inappropriateness 1.599 (p=0.047), abnormal perception/thought content 2.259; the p5 text confirms. One nuance the ground could carry: P-989's discussion (p9) does argue that profile subgroups "might be more sensitive prognostic marker of AD than individual MBI domains", so P-989 does favour aggregation; the ground's point that it is not aggregation-only remains correct, and P-997 takes no position on the question, so no opposition arises. (3) The complex cluster's 45 single-domain members (16.4%) are stated on p4 and no hazard by number of domains appears anywhere; "dose-response" is the record's gloss, not a tested result. (4) The record's resolution and resolution_note say exactly what the ground states. (5) Impulse-type numbers verified (HR 1.920 [1.444-2.554]; OR 1.173 [0.830-1.659], p=0.366); depression OR 2.575 [1.771-3.744] verified on p3. "Significance-only difference" is a fair label since the intervals overlap and the metric types differ. (6) Populations, outcomes and dataset families are as stated; the pack's registry rows confirm T4/T4, V2/V2 and the modality_subtype split (multimodal_MRI vs neuropsychological_scores_only). None of the grounds is wrong or materially overstated.

(lines 545-547). All page attributions are correct.
C-235.defects_check: All eight record_defects are correct against the papers. Verified: no hazard by number of domains in P-989 and 45 single-domain patients inside the complex cluster (defect 1); no count or aggregation analysis in P-997, whose limitations (p6) name symptom co-occurrence as something it could not differentiate (defect 2); the ICD result is HVLT-R recognition discrimination only, beta -0.280 [-0.552, -0.009] p=0.043, with delayed free recall 0.071 p=0.615, and the p5 results text self-contradicts by listing recognition discrimination among the non-significant tests (defect 3); Table 4 per-domain HRs all significant (defect 4); outcomes and populations differ (defect 5); two recruitment sites named on p3 (defect 6); registry rows show T4/T4 and V2/V2, so "all four deterministic gates fail" is overstated, only dataset family and modality_subtype differ (defect 7); P-989 modality_subtype "multimodal_MRI" reflects the n=202 MRI subset (214 scanned, 12 excluded; Table 5 n=55+47+100) while the prognostic analysis uses NPI-Q domains only, and its primary metric is a hazard ratio (defect 8). Two calibration notes rather than errors: defect 3 should acknowledge that P-997's own abstract states "Apathy and ICDs were separately associated with a progressive decline in processing speed-attention and memory, respectively", so the record's "ICDs accelerate memory decline" echoes the paper's abstract and is an overstatement relative to the body, not a fabrication; and defect 6 is minor, since Dongjak-Gu Center for Dementia is a district centre tied to Boramae, though the paper does name two sites. One omission: P-997's registry primary_metric_type is also "not reported" and should be regression beta / odds ratio; the verdict flags this only for P-989.
C-235.would_change: A same-quantity, opposite-direction result in either paper, which neither contains: P-997 reporting a hazard or odds of cognitive-status conversion for a symptom cluster or symptom count, or P-989 reporting per-symptom cognitive-score slopes, in a population and outcome that overlaps the other paper. The affective-only-cluster null in P-989 (HR 1.214 [0.883-1.670]) set against P-997's depression OR 2.575 [1.771-3.744] is the only pair of non-overlapping intervals across the two papers; if the adjudicator chose to treat that as the contested quantity, the outcome would move to documented_incommensurability (HR for AD-dementia conversion in aMCI vs OR for PD-MCI occurrence in de novo PD; a depression/anxiety-only cluster vs any GDS-15>=5 depression), not to genuine.

C-242.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category under the brief's ordering. The record is, in its own words, a "PRE-EMPTIVE INCOMMENSURABILITY RULING on a pair the pipeline will generate": it asserts no disagreement, only that a cross-pair performance comparison would be invalid. That is the "filed note" case the brief lists under outcome 1. Read against the PDFs, there is also no incompatibility to find: P-709 reports FSST time discriminating self-reported 12-month fallers from non-fallers within 46 CDR-0.5 MCI participants (AUC 0.825, cut-off 15.11 s, p. 3); P-1013 reports chest-worn postural-sway measures discriminating its fall criterion in 20 young healthy adults plus 20 MMSE-20-23 older adults (AUC 0.82-0.94 with 95% CIs, Table 2, p. 9). Both are positive, same-direction, in-sample ROC results on different instruments, different reference standards and different populations; neither paper tests or cites the other or claims an ordering. Genuine is impossible on these facts; unresolved and partially_resolved do not apply because there is no disagreement to settle. The only live alternative is documented_incommensurability, which fits the record's substantive content (different estimands) and is what the record itself requested and what the operator's 2026-09-14 annotation wanted preserved to stop the pair regenerating. The brief says to apply the outcomes in order, so false_positive takes precedence, and the verdict file carries the incommensurability content forward in quantity_a/quantity_b, endpoint_and_metric and its explicit fallback sentence. I would add one note for the adjudicator: whichever label is filed, the record's substantive routing content (reference standard, population behind the MCI label, instrument) should travel with it as gate notes, since a bare "false_positive" status would not by itself block a regenerated P-709 x P-1013 candidate.
C-242.grounds_check: All five grounds are supported. (1) "Record asserts no disagreement / pre-emptive filing": verbatim from the record's conflict_statement. (2) "Both results point the same way and the AUCs overlap": P-709 AUC 0.825 (p. 3, no CI printed); P-1013 AUC 0.82-0.94 (p. 8, Table 2 p. 9). 0.825 lies within P-1013's range and inside all four TUG-criterion CIs (0.69-0.96, 0.68-0.96, 0.74-0.98, 0.70-0.97) and two of four BBS CIs (AP 0.82-0.99, V 0.81-0.99); it falls below the ML-BBS and mean-BBS lower bounds (0.87, 0.84). The verdict file wisely cites a TUG interval as its example; "the AUCs overlap" is accurate for the range and most intervals, and P-709 prints no CI, so the claim is fair rather than overstated. (3) "Different instruments, neither claims an ordering": P-709's ROC is on the FSST only (TUG/BBS appear only as concurrent-validity correlates); P-1013 tests the PSD wearable with BBS/TUG as criteria. Neither cites the other. Correct. (4) "Fallback would be documented_incommensurability, never genuine": reference standards differ (12-month recalled falls vs BBS < 40 / TUG > 14 s or 3-month falls), populations differ (neurologist CDR 0.5, mean age 71.7, vs MMSE 20-23 + ABC + recent fall, mean age 79, pooled with 20 adults aged 25), instruments differ. Correct. (5) "Record misreads sources on P-1013 positives and metric type": both verified (see defects). Gate assessments: task T4 match and validation V2 match confirmed in the pack registry rows; performance_suspect false for both papers confirmed in index.json; independence confirmed (Turkish vs Korean teams, no shared authors; Sao Carlos group cited by both as P-709 ref 8 and P-1013 ref 25 only). Two low-stakes observations that do not affect the verdict: calling two independent single-site original cohorts a "dataset_family mismatch" and calling clinical-motor-scale vs wearable-sensor a "modality family" (rather than subtype) mismatch are judgment calls about gate granularity; the machine output in the record fails modality_subtype, not a family gate. Neither changes anything because the verdict does not rest on the gates.
C-242.quote_check: All ten evidence quotes located verbatim in the extracts at the stated pages: P-709 p. 3 (12-month fall history definition, lines 210-211; cut-off 15.11 s / AUC 0.825 / 77.38% / 89.50%, lines 294-296), p. 5 (cut-off marks high fall risk, lines 511-513), p. 6 (recall bias caveat, lines 567-569); P-1013 p. 1 (sens 0.82-0.99 / spec 0.69-0.90 / acc 0.53-0.81), p. 2 (20 healthy adults 25.20 +/- 3.19 and 20 MCI 79.00 +/- 8.25; MMSE 20-23 and at least one fall in past 3 months), p. 5 (Sec. 2.4 BBS < 40 / TUG > 14 s criterion; Sec. 2.5 falls-within-3-months positives), p. 8 (AUC 0.82-0.94, Table 2). The three load-bearing quotes, each confirmed: the P-709 p. 3 AUC 0.825 sentence; the P-1013 p. 8 AUC 0.82-0.94 sentence (which establishes metric-type compatibility and same-direction overlap); and the pair of P-1013 p. 5 criterion definitions (which establish that the paper is internally inconsistent about what its positives are, and therefore that the record's "never falls at all" is overstated). Supporting numbers in what_each_reports also check out: Fig. 3 caption sensitivity 77.8% (P-709 line 559), median FSST 17.02 vs 14.00 s (Table 4), 22 fallers / 24 non-fallers (Table 1), no AUC CI anywhere in P-709; P-1013 Table 3 has seven of eight rows with accuracy strictly below both sensitivity and specificity (the BBS-V row has accuracy equal to specificity, so "7 of 8" is exactly right), and the specificity formula is printed as TN/(TN+FN) on p. 5.
C-242.defects_check: All five record_defects are correct against the papers. (1) The two sentences the record attributes to P-709 ("it does not predict anything"; "contaminated by the very deficit that defines the exposure group") appear nowhere in the P-709 PDF; the paper's own caveat is recall bias "underestimating fall frequency" (p. 6) and its authors present the cut-off as marking high fall risk (p. 5, and the Conclusion calls it "strong fall differentiation skills"). The record's conflict_statement calls the first sentence "its own appraisal" and its evidence_quotes file it as a P-709 quote with "All 8 quotes verified verbatim"; that verification was against summary blocks, not the PDF. The underlying facts (baseline 12-month self-report, p. 3; cut-off derived and evaluated in the same 46, no validation set) are correct as the verdict says. (2) "P-1013's positives are never falls at all" is too strong: Sec. 2.5 defines positives as participants who "experienced falls within 3 months"; only Sec. 2.4 names BBS/TUG cut-offs. The paper is internally inconsistent, and because Table 3's accuracies are arithmetically impossible one cannot reverse-engineer which criterion was actually applied. (3) The AUC_ROC-vs-Accuracy metric warning is a coding artefact: P-1013 Table 2 reports ROC AUCs with 95% CIs. This also exposes a registry defect worth logging: P-1013's row has primary_metric_type "Accuracy" and Best_Metric "accuracy 0.53-0.81", figures its own Table 3 cannot support, while the paper's headline discrimination result is AUC 0.82-0.94. (4) "both are single-site MCI cohorts of comparable size" is wrong for P-1013 (half the sample is young healthy adults; MCI defined by MMSE 20-23 + ABC + a recent fall, not a clinical diagnosis); the record is internally inconsistent here, since it states the 25-vs-79 age gap later in the same paragraph. (5) P-695: "null in every stratum" is right for any fall (Table 3: 0.185 / 0.232 / 0.528), but Table 4 reports recurrent falls in MCI at p = 0.017 with OR 13147.598 (5.582-30969485), and P-695's own results text attaches p = 0.185 and OR 31.718 to MCI and OR 31.353 to AD, shifted one column from its Table 3; the verdict describes this exactly. One small addition the list omits: the record's remaining P-1013 and P-709 "quotes" are also summary-block paraphrases rather than PDF text (e.g. "Cross-sectional design against clinical tests rather than real falls; young-control half of sample limits MCI-specific inference"), though their factual content is accurate; only the two flagged in defect 1 are materially misattributed as the paper's own words.
C-242.would_change: The category would move to documented_incommensurability, not genuine, if the adjudicator's convention for pre-emptive routing notes is to file them under the category the note requests (the record asks for DI and the operator's 2026-09-14 annotation wanted that content preserved against regeneration); the substance is identical either way. It could only become genuine if a source in the corpus tested the FSST and the wearable on the same fall outcome in the same population class with an opposite result, or if one of these papers reported that its instrument fails to discriminate fallers in MCI; neither PDF contains such a result.

C-236.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category and should stand. The ledger record itself carries genuine_conflict:false and resolution "Both findings stand", and its description presents P-988 (eye-tracking during VSTMB predicts MCI-to-ADS) and P-991 (MMSE/CDT/VVT scores predict progression poorly) as both true, then reframes the pair as a design lesson. That is the "architectural fork" the brief lists under outcome 1, and outcome 1 is applied first. The papers confirm there is no disagreement to adjudicate: the two studies evaluate different instruments on different endpoints (P-988: baseline oculomotor model vs clinically defined ADS within 40 months in 65 MCI patients, Bahia Blanca; P-991: baseline paper-test scores vs next-stage conversion over 12-48 months in 117 returners, plus MCI-to-AD ROC in 76 MCI, Vienna), and neither paper tests or makes a claim about the other's instrument. On the record's own question (can a brief clinic test carry prognostic signal?) both answer yes to some degree: P-988 AUC 0.95 for MCI vs MCI_C (p7), P-991 MMSE AUC 0.808 within MCI (p6) with the authors' conclusion that "solely the MMSE showed some validity" (p10). Neither paper reports confidence intervals for these prognostic AUCs, so no incompatibility could be shown from reported uncertainty even if one treated the instruments as one quantity. Genuine is excluded on several independent grounds (different estimand, dataset-family and modality-family gates unmatched with no waiver on record, and P-988's in-sample AUC 1.0 in a single-site n=65 cohort). If the adjudicator insists on reading the record as asserting a disagreement, the fallback is documented_incommensurability, as the reader states; it is not genuine under any reading.
C-236.grounds_check: Ground 1 (record presents both findings as true, architectural fork): supported by the record text verbatim ("Both findings stand", genuine_conflict false). Ground 2 (different instruments, neither tests the other's): supported; P-988 administers MMSE and ACE-R at baseline but reports only group means (Section 3.1, p3) and no prognostic analysis of them; P-991 records no eye movements. C-253.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. Read against the sources, the two papers point in opposite directions only under the shared label 'cholinergic therapy and MCI-to-AD conversion'. P-1216 (Liu et al., ADNI, n=558) estimates an IPTW-adjusted time-varying Cox HR of 1.77 (1.15-2.73) for progression to NINCDS-ADRDA AD dementia over up to 120 months among users of donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine (p.3, p.5, Table 2). P-1215 (Biggio and Mencacci, narrative review) relays, second-hand and without any test statistic, a 3-year conversion contrast of 8.2% vs 26.1% for choline alphoscerate vs no therapy from Ponomareva 2024, plus an unquantified reduced-conversion statement from Kim 2025 (p.6), and concludes the precursor 'may also be useful as a preventive therapy' (p.8). Different exposure (cholinesterase inhibitor vs cholinergic precursor), different metric type (hazard ratio vs crude proportions), different horizon (10 y vs 3 y), and task and dataset-family gates that fail with no waiver on record: this is exactly the brief's definition of incommensurability, and the reclassification pattern of precedents C-80/C-204/C-227/C-232/C-234. Genuine is excluded outright by the exposure difference; partially_resolved does not arise because there is no comparable quantity to bridge. The only serious alternative is false_positive under the clause 'the record describes no disagreement', because the operator's 2026-09-14 revision made the record disclaim any disagreement. I would not take that route: the record was filed as, and still is, a two-paper record in which an apparent opposition under a shared label is dissolved by showing the quantities differ, which is the incommensurability outcome, not a filed note, an architectural fork or a single-paper record. One detail the verdict file did not use strengthens the horizon ground: P-1216 p.10 states 'while initial conversion rates were similar between groups, ChEI users demonstrated significantly higher rates of progression from MCI to AD dementia compared to non-users after 6 years of follow-up', so at P-1215's 3-year horizon P-1216 itself reports no separation.

C-255.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category and should stand. Read against both PDFs, there is no disagreement to adjudicate: P-1206 (Zhou et al., Front Med 2024) reports a Gal-3 + age + education nomogram with held-out validation AUC 0.775 (0.681-0.870) on n=98; P-1212 (Shen et al., J Diabetes Investig 2025) reports a BVR-A + HOMA-IR + duration nomogram with held-out test-set AUC 0.863 (0.752-0.973) on roughly 42 patients. Each point estimate sits inside the other's 95% interval (0.775 in 0.752-0.973; 0.863 in 0.681-0.870), so even forced onto one quantity the two are compatible. Neither paper measures the other's marker, and neither claims an ordering the other refutes: P-1206's only comparison is nomogram vs Gal-3 alone (p=0.002 in training); P-1212's ranking claims (p.6 'BVR-A is more advantageous than HOMA-IR', p.7 'Among the indicators studied, BVR-A had the highest efficiency') cover only its own three indicators. The ledger record itself states 'no head-to-head and no disagreement in direction', which is the brief's 'record describes no disagreement' clause. Under the brief's ordered outcomes false_positive is reached first and applies; documented_incommensurability (the record's own label) would also be defensible on the disjoint-predictor-set test but is second in order, and the verdict file already notes this alternative. No reading makes it genuine. The registry's AUC_ROC vs C_index split is confirmed a coding artefact: for a binary logistic nomogram the C-statistic is the ROC-AUC, and P-1212 prints the same 0.863 under both names while P-1206's 'optimism-corrected C-index' 0.813 (0.757-0.868) matches its training AUC 0.813 (0.758-0.867). Performance-validity exclusion not triggered: highest reported figures are 0.897 (P-1212 training) and a single CV fold at 0.964; neither row is flagged. Independence confirmed: different centres (Nanjing vs Xuzhou, both Jiangsu), non-overlapping enrolment windows, no shared authors (Xueling Zhou vs Xiaoyan Zhou; Shaohua Wang vs Nan Wang are different people).
C-255.grounds_check: All five grounds are supported by the PDFs. Ground 1 (no disagreement; record's own words): correct; the record's conflict_statement reason (1) says exactly 'there is no head-to-head and no disagreement in direction'. Ground 2 (overlapping held-out estimates): arithmetic checked and correct under either of P-1212's printed upper bounds (0.973 or 0.937). Ground 3 (record misreads P-1212's validation): correct. P-1212 p.3 states the 7:3 split with the training set used 'to screen variables and construct the predictive model' and the test set 'to validate the results', then gives test-set AUC 0.863 (0.752-0.973); the 5-fold CV is a separate analysis with mean AUC 0.884 (folds 0.738-0.964). The wide single-marker CIs (BVR-A 0.655-0.926) are consistent with a ~42-patient test set rather than n=140, which further supports the held-out reading. One small imprecision: 'the same design P-1206 used' glosses that P-1206 used stratified sampling for its split (p.4) while P-1212 does not state stratification; immaterial to the point. Ground 4 (ranking claims confined to own indicators): correct; no comparative test (DeLong or otherwise) appears anywhere in P-1212. Ground 5 (would not be one quantity anyway): predictor sets are disjoint; MoCA cut-offs differ in that P-1212 defines MCI as 19-25 (upper bound identical, lower bound excludes <19), so 'differ' is accurate but the difference is minor, and the verdict's endpoint field rightly says 'slightly'. The dataset-family 'mismatch' reading (two distinct own cohorts) matches how every sibling round-18 reading and precedent C-01 (ADNI subset vs Moscow cohort, dataset_family_equivalence false) apply the gate, so it is not overstated relative to the rule as applied; I note only that this reading makes any two own-cohort studies fail the gate absent a waiver, which is a property of the gate the adjudicator may wish to keep in view given the external critic's objection. It does not bear on this verdict, which rests on grounds 1-2. One phrase in what_would_change is slightly under-stated rather than overstated: P-1206's unadjusted duration OR 1.045 (1.006-1.087) 'points the same way' as P-1212's 1.407 (1.163-1.701), but the intervals do not overlap; the comparison still fails the same-quantity test because P-1212's figure is from a multivariable stepwise model (with HOMA-IR and BVR-A, age and education dropped) and the cohorts' duration ranges differ sharply (P-1212 medians 4 vs 7 years; P-1206 10 vs 10 years with a >=3-year entry criterion), so per-year ORs are not comparable estimands. That observation is correctly kept outside this record's claim.

C-256.verdict_assessment: false_positive stands. Read against the PDFs there is no disagreement to adjudicate. (1) P-1093 reports the very trajectory the record attributes to P-1000 as the 'observed arm' (MCI $2,430.3 -> $1,975.1 -> $2,048.9, 'increased modestly' from 6 to 36 months; discussion p.12 'remained relatively stable through 36 months') in the same paper as its +$8,504 estimate, so both results are presented as true together by the same authors on the same 617 patients. (2) The +$8,504 is the GLM-implied increment in cumulative 36-month cost at the MMRM LSMC of -2.1 versus no decline, fitted across 108 MCI completers (Table 4: coefficient -0.046, SE 0.019; exp(0.046 x 2.1) - 1 = 10.2%, matching the paper). A positive between-patient gradient of cumulative cost on MMSE change is compatible with a flat cohort-mean monthly cost after a post-diagnosis fall; the record's own residual_risk concedes 'not logically contradictory'. (3) P-1000 does not claim progression fails to raise costs: p.9 'the trend toward rising indirect caregiver costs among patients with MCI and MILD over 36 months show the additional economic impact associated with clinical progression'. P-1093 p.10 in turn reads the earlier 36-month GERAS-US report as evidence of 'an increase in the total societal costs and caregiver burden as the disease progresses', i.e. the later paper treats the earlier one as concordant (slightly overstating it, since P-1000 reports total costs steady and only components rising). (4) The record describes itself as citation hygiene and 'EXPLICITLY NOT A GENUINE CONFLICT'; under the brief a filed note with no disagreement is step 1. documented_incommensurability is a defensible alternative label (cohort-mean monthly trajectory versus between-patient cumulative-cost gradient in a completer subset), but the brief applies false_positive first and the incompatible_if_same test is 'No', so incommensurability is not what dissolves the pair. Not genuine on two independent counts: no incompatible results, and the pair is two analyses of one study (identical N=617/300/317, identical baseline MCI cost $2,430, same first author and sponsor, P-1093 citing P-1000 as [26]). The only same-quantity discrepancy in the PDFs, the MCI MMSE decline (P-1000: about 1 point, 'not significant', from Figure 1 'actual scores'; P-1093: MMRM LSMC -2.1 (-2.9, -1.3), p<0.001), is not the record's claim, sits within one cohort and author group, is a significance/estimator difference (observed completer means versus MMRM extrapolating the sicker dropouts), and the brief says a significance difference is not a data conflict; the verdict rightly parks it as a separate within-study note.
C-256.grounds_check: Grounds 1, 2, 3 and 5 are fully supported by the PDFs (P-1093 pp.7, 8, 12, 13; P-1000 p.9; Table 4). Two grounds are overstated in wording though not in effect. Ground 4 ('the record's premise that costs stayed flat despite a documented MCI decline misreads P-1000'): P-1000 does document a decline in MCI, 'only a modest decline of 1 point on the MMSE' (p.4) and CFI worsening (p.4 'In both patients with MCI and those with MILD, the mean MMSE and mean CFI scores demonstrated worsening'), alongside flat costs; what P-1000 does not report is a meaningful or significant MCI decline (highlights: 'not for those with MCI'; p.7 'patients with MCI did not'). The ground should say the record overstates the magnitude and significance of the MCI decline, not that P-1000 reports no decline. Ground 6 ('could not be independent arms of a contradiction in any case') is stronger than the rule, which says shared cohort or authorship is 'recorded as non-independence' and the brief adds 'not disqualifying'; here the two papers analyse literally the same 617 patients so 'two analyses of one study' is fair, but the ground should be framed as non-independence recorded, with the verdict carried by grounds 1-3. Minor: 'P-1093 cites P-1000 as its reference [26] for the cost trajectory' is slightly loose; [26] is cited on p.12 for the explanation of the initial cost decline and on p.3 for RUD methods, not for the trajectory numbers themselves. The independence field's 'sponsor (Eli Lilly)' is confirmed by both funding statements.

C-259.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. P-845 (Brooks et al., ARR 102, 2024) is a narrative review with no pooled estimate, no effect size and no between-modality test anywhere in the paper; its Table 1 (p3) is a qualitative tally of 34 RCTs with Yes/No/N/A cells for ADL and NPI. Its aerobic-first verdict (abstract, p1) rests on cognitive domains and independent living; the conclusion (p9) extends it only as 'has the potential to ... decrease psychiatric symptoms' and 'very little evidence that non-aerobic exercise provides these beneficial effects', an evidence-volume statement. P-848 (Kong et al., ARR 112, 2025) reports SMDs against active control for NPS: resistance -1.70 (-3.12, -0.29) from three dementia/AD trials, multi-component -0.70 (-1.32, -0.08), all other comparisons non-significant (p8). Under the rule, 'incompatible' requires opposite directions each supported by the study's own statistics or intervals that exclude each other; P-845 supplies no statistic, so nothing in P-848 can be excluded by it and genuine is unavailable. Metric type is incommensurable (narrative ordinal verdict vs SMD), the outcome behind the headline claims differs (cognition/ADL vs NPS), and the modality nodes differ (Holthoff 2015 is Aerobic in P-845 Table 1 and Resistance in P-848 Table 1; Hoffmann 2016 is Aerobic vs Multi-component; Fajersztajn 2008 is Non-Aerobic vs Multi-component). On the one outcome both bear on quantitatively, cognition, P-848 finds no significant differences between exercise types (p8), so no aerobic-first reading is refuted. I considered false_positive: the record does describe a nominal disagreement (different optimal-modality nominations), so it is not a 'no disagreement' record; the disagreement dissolves because the quantities differ, which is category 2 by the brief's own definition. P-848 itself agrees with P-845 on the evidence-volume point ('due to the limited number of studies on resistance exercise, these findings should be interpreted with caution', p1), so there is no incompatibility even qualitatively. Not a performance comparison; performance-validity flag irrelevant. Gates as stated in the file are correct (T6/T6; both pool exercise RCTs in cognitive impairment with at least eight shared trials; validation n/a; exercise family matched but nodes mismatched).
C-259.grounds_check: All five grounds are supported by the papers; two are anchored more weakly than the file suggests. Ground 1 (different outcomes behind the best-modality claims) is correct for the abstract verdict [q1, p1 lines 23-24] and P-848's NPS ranking [q7, p1 line 29]; the file itself qualifies it in quantity_a and defect 1 by noting the p9 conclusion touches psychiatric symptoms, so it is not overstated in context. Ground 2 (P-845 produces no estimate) is TRUE on a full read (no effect size, CI or test anywhere; Table 1 cells are Yes/No/Lack of Decline), BUT the cited anchor q4 'No data was used for the research described in the article' is Elsevier data-availability boilerplate: P-848, a 3655-participant NMA, prints the identical sentence at p12 line 1649. q4 therefore proves nothing about P-845's lack of an estimate; the ground should rest on the whole-paper read and Table 1, not q4. The q3 part of ground 2 (evidence-volume claim) is exactly right; P-845 Section 3.1 (p2) even lists Burgener 2008, a Non-Aerobic trial, among studies where NPS improved, and Table 1 marks its 'Decreased NPI' as Yes, so P-845 never claims non-aerobic exercise fails on NPS. C-257.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category under the brief's ordering. The record's central premise, that the two reviews "reach opposite headline verdicts", is contradicted by P-699 itself: its conclusion (p.7) states that "exergaming improves cognitive and physical function in older adults with MCI or dementia" and its only MCI-only global-cognition pool (MoCA, Amjad 2019 + Liao 2020 + Liu 2022) is significantly positive (MD 2.12, 95% CI 0.53-3.70, P=0.009). The "null arm" the record leans on is the MMSE pool (MD 0.95, 95% CI -1.17 to 3.08, P=0.38), which is a positive point estimate that is merely non-significant, in a pool of four dementia trials plus one MCI trial. Set against P-698's SMD 0.76 (CI 0.37-1.14/0.37-0.91), that is at most a significance-only difference, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict. No reading makes it genuine: both reviews conclude in favour of the intervention, and the narrower "does cognitive loading add value" question is untested on both sides (P-698 Q(1)=2.91, p=0.09; P-699 has no pooled contrast). The only defensible alternative label is documented_incommensurability (different intervention, comparator, metric type, population and disjoint pooled literatures), which the verdict itself flags; C-234 was labelled that way by the operator when both "different quantities" and "compatible results" held. But the round-18 brief explicitly orders false_positive first, and here the record additionally misreads P-699 (invented "primary" designation, three quoted sentences not in the PDF), so false_positive is the better fit. Verdict should stand.

C-260.verdict_assessment: Upheld. Read against both PDFs the two AUCs are estimates of different quantities. P-1225 (Giacomucci 2023, JNS 453:120805) reports AUC 0.910 for plasma p-tau181 separating A+T+ carriers from non-carriers WITHIN SCD and MCI patients, with the AD-dementia group excluded from the ROC ("we did not consider AD-d group (as 100% of these patients were AP+) and we merged SCD and MCI", p.4), no healthy controls ("Secondly, the lack of a healthy control group", p.7), and T status defined by CSF p-tau181 on Lumipulse (p.2-3). P-1231 (Qu 2021, NBR 128:479-486) prints "P-tau 181 (AUC = 0.610-0.840; sensitivity 67-71 %; specificity 66-86 %)" as a narrative range from "the systematic review of 32 eligible studies (Supplementary Table 6)" for "identifying AD and aMCI patients from controls" (p.5); what it actually pools are ratios of means (AD vs controls 2.06 [1.39-3.06]; AD vs aMCI 1.36 [1.20-1.54], p.3). A range of study-level values is not an interval for a common parameter, so a further study at 0.910 on a different target condition contradicts nothing. I tested the routes to genuine that the record did not name: (a) the stage gradient - P-1231 finds AD > aMCI (1.36, 1.20-1.54); P-1225's unadjusted MCI 2.91 vs AD-d 4.03 points the same way (ratio about 1.38) and its "no differences" is a Bonferroni post-hoc non-significance with 14 vs 32 patients, which the Section 5.2 rule excludes; its "not influenced by stage" is an AP-adjusted estimand whose own Diagnosis coefficient is positive with a CI excluding zero (B = 0.415, 0.051-0.778, Table 4), so there is no opposite direction anywhere. (b) Sensitivity 86.36% vs the 67-71% range fails for the same target-condition reason. Three deterministic gates fail with no waiver (T1 vs T6; Florence cohort vs literature to 17 May 2021, which cannot contain a paper recruiting to September 2022; V1 vs V2), which by itself places the pair in category 2. I considered false_positive on the ground that the record is itself a filed incommensurability note; it does not displace DI because the record names a specific apparent numerical collision (0.910 above 0.61-0.84) that the sources dissolve by showing different estimands, which is DI's literal definition, and the two precedents of the same kind (C-238, C-239) were carried as documented_incommensurability. Performance-validity flag on P-1231 correctly judged inapplicable (a synthesis quoting a P-tau217 range, not an internal-validation classifier).

One small overstatement carried over from quantity_b: P-1231's cases are called "CLINICALLY diagnosed"; the paper says only that participants "conformed to AD and MCI diagnostic criteria" (p.2) and does not state whether biomarker-supported criteria were used in any pooled study. C-254.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. I read both PDFs in full and tested the two possible alignments. (a) The record's own alignment sets P-999's class-level aHRs 0.96-0.98 (each class vs non-users of THAT class, who may take other AHMs; P-999 p.9) against P-1157's polypharmacy HR 0.49 (>=5 prescription drugs vs fewer; P-1157 p.3). A drug-class contrast and a medication-count contrast are different exposures, so the disjoint intervals are not a contradiction. (b) The closest like-for-like alignment, which the record omits, is P-1157's per-category 'antihypertensive agents' HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) (p.5) against P-999's any-AHM-vs-none aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08) (p.14, Table 3). These point opposite ways with disjoint intervals, so they WOULD be incompatible if they were the same quantity. They are not: P-999 restricted the cohort to hypertensives precisely so the comparator would be untreated hypertensives ('including normotensive patients ... would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled', p.9), whereas P-1157's non-users are mostly the 83 of 237 participants without hypertension, its model carries no hypertension term (covariate list p.4), and hypertension itself is associated with LESS progression in that cohort (72.3% vs 52.8%, p=0.003, Table 2; derived 47/154 hypertensive vs 42/83 non-hypertensive progressed, crude ratio about 0.60, the same size as the AHM HR 0.59). Both results can be true at once: hypertension status tracks slower progression in Kaohsiung, and treated vs untreated hypertensives in Optum differ little. The rule lists 'population behind the shared label' and comparison as parts of the estimand, so this is category 2, not a confounding critique of one arm. Secondary differences reinforce it: P-999 adjusts for statin and metformin and its estimate swings from 0.84 (0.80-0.88) with statins to 1.11 (1.08-1.13) without (Table 5), while P-1157 adjusts for no co-medication and its interval contains P-999's statin-user figure; P-999's exposure is consumption 'during the study period', P-1157's a baseline prescription. Not genuine: no pairing is on one quantity. Not false_positive: the record does describe a numerical gap that would be incompatible if the quantity were shared, and the brief directs different-quantity cases to category 2. Not partially_resolved: neither reader found a bridging third study and none is needed since the explanation is the quantity. Not unresolved: the PDFs settle it. Performance-validity exclusion does not arise (not a performance comparison; both rows performance_suspect false). Independence confirmed (different countries, data, authors; neither cites the other).
C-254.grounds_check: Ground 1 (exposures differ on the record's framing): supported; P-999 p.9 defines class non-users as 'may or may not consume AHMs from other drug classes', P-1157 p.3 defines polypharmacy as >=5 prescriptions. Ground 2 (like-for-like 0.59 vs 1.06 differs in comparator population; P-1157 has no hypertension covariate and hypertension is commoner among non-progressors): supported on every point; I recomputed 154/237 = 65.0% hypertensive from Table 1 (68+86) and confirmed the covariate list on p.4 has no hypertension term (Charlson CCI does not include hypertension). Ground 3 (estimate depends on comparator and co-medication; P-1157 adjusts for no medication; exposure windows differ): supported by Tables 3 and 5 and P-1157 p.4 'All Cox regression models were adjusted for the same covariates listed above'. One caution the first reader did not note: P-999's Table 4 and Table 5 footnotes give stratum sizes (metformin Y N=107,127; statin Y N=59,980) that contradict Table 1 (21,556 metformin users; 68,703 statin users), so the Y/N counts in those footnotes are swapped. The narrative text (p.17: protective 'under consumption of Statins', harmful 'under non-consumption') and the interval widths both place 0.84 in the statin-user stratum, so the reading in ground 3 stands, but the adjudicator should know P-999 has this internal labelling error. Ground 4 (dataset-family gate fails, no waiver): factually true but the weakest ground and, if it stood alone, overstated: two independent cohorts will always differ in dataset family, and a waiver would be routine here (the challenger says the same). The verdict does not rest on it and I would not cite it as a reason in the manuscript. Ground 5 (no pairing estimates the same quantity): follows from grounds 1-3. Nothing in the grounds is wrong; the 'what_each_reports' block is accurate throughout, including its correct catch that the Methods print COPD codes (ICD-9 491.x/492.x/496; ICD-10 J41-J44) as the hypertension definition and G31.83 under both MCI and Lewy-body dementia, which Table 1's COPD prevalence of 29.6-36.8% shows to be a transcription error rather than the actual restriction.

(3) P-999 p.9 'the study population was narrowed down from patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to hypertensive patients with MCI.' together with the challenger's p.9 quote 'including normotensive patients with MCI to our population would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled as very few normotensive patients are taking AHMs.' (4) P-1157 p.4 covariate list with no hypertension term, and p.4 'participants who progressed to dementia had a lower prevalence of hypertension (p = 0.003)'. C-254.defects_check: All seven listed defects are correct against the record and the PDFs. (1) 'versus non-use'/'against non-use': the record text says this and P-999's class comparator is non-users of that class; against no AHM at all the figure is 1.06. Valid. (2) 'essentially at the null': Table 3 intervals exclude 1 for diuretics and CCBs and touch 1.00 for the rest; the authors call them significant protective effects. The record's gloss is interpretive, not what the paper reports. Valid. (3) 'subgroup reading carrying no between-class test': P-1157 fits separate adjusted Cox models per medication category and reports HRs with CIs (p.5); these are not subgroups of the polypharmacy model. Valid and material, since these are the numbers a synthesis would set against P-999. C-261.verdict_assessment: Upheld. The record sets P-824's RuLAS 5-year ROC-AUC 0.823 (external cohort, test-free 13-item composite, 'MCI' = HDS < 21.5 at follow-up) against P-981's RS1/RS2 AUC 0.64-0.70 for '~3-year incident MCI'. Read in full, P-981 computes RS1/RS2 in the 5,921-person baseline cross-section (Table 1: 1,174 MCI vs 4,747 NC; p3 defines discrimination as distinguishing NC from MCI individuals; Table 3 occurrence rates 2.98-47.08% match the 19.8% prevalence, not the 7.8% incidence; Figure 1A CIs of +/-0.02 fit n=5,921, not 72 events - I recomputed the Hanley-McNeil SE: 0.009 for the cross-section vs 0.036 for 72/849). Its only incident-MCI estimate is RS3 (0.785, p5), which contains MMSE plus three neuropsychological test scores, against a two-expert Petersen consensus diagnosis, over a Table 4 mean follow-up of 2.0-2.25 years, apparent validation only. So the quantities differ on endpoint construct (single global-screen cut-off vs consensus memory-only MCI), case type (prevalent vs incident for the figures cited), predictor set (test-free vs cognitive tests included), horizon, dataset family and validation tier, with no waiver on record. Either non-genuine category leaves the genuine count unchanged; incommensurability is the more informative and the correct one under the rule. Performance-validity flag correctly not triggered (max 0.861, apparent, CHARLS). Both PDFs are the right papers (P-824 Jin et al JAMDA 2023, doi 10.1016/j.jamda.2023.08.016; P-981 Li et al Front Aging Neurosci 2022, 976126).

C-262.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. Both papers report a C-index for a Cox model of MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, so the metric type matches and the pair looks comparable on the registry columns. On the PDFs the two C-indices are estimates of different quantities on every axis the brief names. (1) Population behind the label: P-13's 0.844 is confined to a high-risk subgroup (340 of 718; 80.9% LMCI, Table 3) chosen by HDDC clustering of longitudinal FAQ trajectories, i.e. with follow-up information, and then to its 237-patient training split (Table 4 header 'n = 237'); P-1128 keeps 68 converters within 6-60 months plus 94 patients stable for 5 years and excludes reverters (p.2). P-13 itself shows how much the subgroup moves a C-index: baseline ADAS13 scores 0.677 in the high-risk and 0.825 in the low-risk group (pp.3-4). (2) Predictor set and input representation: P-13 uses MFPCA trajectory scores of longitudinal CDRSB and hippocampal volume plus baseline ADAS13, MMSE, RAVLT, FAQ, demographics and APOE e4 (p.4, Table 4); P-1128 uses 37 baseline whole-cortex morphology and gray-matter-network radiomics features plus MoCA and FAQ (p.3, p.7). (3) Horizon: visits to 96 months (p.2) against 6-60 months with 5-year follow-up (p.2, p.8). (4) Evaluation level: P-13's headline 0.844 is the apparent training C-index (0.829 optimism-corrected, 0.805 test, p.4); P-1128's headline 0.951 is training with 0.880 on a 50-patient hold-out (Table 2). Not genuine: under the rule, 'two different methods each reporting a different score where neither study claims the ordering the other refutes' is not incompatible, and no ordering claim is refuted. P-1128's 'higher accuracy' claim (p.7) is made against its refs 7 (Li et al. 2019, C-index 0.864) and 9 (Barnes et al. 2014, 0.78), not against P-13, which it does not cite; P-13's 'longitudinal beats baseline' is within its own markers and P-1128 tests no longitudinal model ('did not analyze dynamic follow-up data', p.8); P-13's hippocampus sentence (p.5) cites Teipel et al. 2013. Shared ADNI participants make this non-independence, not a contradiction. Why not false_positive: the FP triggers 'record misreads its paper' and 'filed note' do apply by the letter, but the face-value results are not compatible (training 0.951, 0.928-0.974, against 0.844, 0.815-0.873, non-overlapping) and the gap fails on quantity, which is exactly the DI definition; the record's own filed status is DI; and the round treated the other filed notes the same way (C-253, C-260 read as DI; closed precedents C-238, C-239 filed as DI). If the operator prefers filed EXAMINED NON-CONFLICT notes labelled false_positive, C-262 should move together with C-253 and C-260, not alone; that is a labelling convention, not an error in this reading. Partially_resolved and unresolved do not fit: there is no comparable-quantity disagreement to bridge, and the sources do settle it.

C-263.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability should stand. Read in full, the two papers report on different populations and different constructs: P-1017 reports self-reported role share and tool use among 50 US psychiatrists on an opt-in commercial panel, each required to have seen at least 25 MCI/mild AD patients in the past month (p3), and its favourable sentence ("They can provide timely and accurate diagnosis", p1) is an authors' conclusion with no accuracy measured anywhere in the paper (the word "accuracy" does not occur outside that conclusion). P-1080 reports proportions among 121 Italian neurologists at 17 deliberately chosen centres and 203 of their patients, and its "suboptimal management" (p1, p8) is a normative inference from non-uniform criteria and under-use of MoCA, biomarkers and rehabilitation; it explicitly excluded psychiatrists (p8). The contested "quantity" the record names, whether specialist MCI practice is adequate, is measured by neither paper, so the surface disagreement is between authorial framings about different clinician populations in different countries, which is "a claim about X set against a claim about Y" and cannot be genuine. On the one measured item both papers share, use of a brief cognitive screen, they agree (94% vs 93.3%). The only credible alternative is false_positive on the "flatly concordant" reading the record's own residual_risk anticipates; it loses on the brief's wording (false_positive presupposes compatible results on the same quantity or a record that describes no disagreement, whereas this record describes a surface disagreement that dissolves because the quantities differ) and on the round's convention (C-238, C-239 and this round's C-237, C-253, C-254, C-260, C-261, C-265 kept self-filed incommensurability records in that category). Neither category changes the review's count. Not genuine under any reading: no shared estimand, no uncertainty on either side, and the dataset-family gate fails without a waiver.

Three small defects the verdict did not list: the record's verification block states "All 8 quotes verified verbatim", which is false against the PDFs (seven of eight are not PDF text; the sweep verified summary blocks, not the papers); the conflict_statement's quoted phrase 'suboptimal and inconsistent MCI management in Italy' is not P-1080's wording (the paper says "suboptimal management of MCI patients in Italy" and, separately, "non-uniform" and "heterogeneous"); and the record's first P-1017 quote and P-1080 phase-1 quote are non-verbatim paraphrases, factually faithful but not quotations.
