C-263.would_change: A second survey estimating the same proportion in the same clinician class (for example, the share of neurologists in one country who personally make the MCI diagnosis, or who use a named test) with an estimate whose uncertainty excluded the other paper's, and a claim in one paper that the other's figure is wrong. Nothing in these two papers does that; P-1017's US neurologist figures (75%/74% personally diagnosing, 84% advanced training) and P-1080's Italian neurologist figures (83.1% use the MCI category, 97.5% MRI) are different items and neither reports uncertainty. I would move to false_positive only if the adjudicator rules that a record self-filed as incommensurability, whose only shared measured item is concordant, describes no disagreement at all; the review's count is unaffected either way.

C-237.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. The two AUCs are estimates for different predictors: P-1232's figure (0.700, CI 0.641-0.760, p5) is the in-sample ROC of a logistic combination of three exosomal lncRNAs in 150 MCI v 150 controls; P-1254's figure (0.901, p1) is the in-sample ROC of a single literature-preselected exosomal miRNA in 24 MCI v 24 controls (Fig 4e legend, p7; sens 79.2% = 19/24). Neither paper measures the other's markers, and the rule names predictor set as a quantity difference. The populations behind the shared label also differ: education-specific MMSE cut-offs with age/sex-matched controls (mean MMSE 18.46 v 28.15, Table 1 p3) against MoCA < 26 plus EADC criteria with controls averaging 4.8 years younger than cases (73.35 v 78.12, Table 3 p4). Genuine is excluded: an AUC is a property of a specific classifier, and no ordering claim crosses the papers. P-1232's only lncRNA-versus-miRNA sentence (p8) is derived from 'a broader range of biological functions' and concerns research scope, not accuracy (P-1232 measured no miRNA); P-1254 contains zero occurrences of 'lncRNA' or 'LINC' (grep confirmed). partially_resolved_candidate is excluded because the quantities are not comparable and no third corpus study measures these markers (all 16 summaries.md hits for the five marker names lie inside the P-1232 and P-1254 blocks). unresolved is excluded because the papers are explicit about what each measured. The only defensible alternative is false_positive under outcome 1(c), since the record uses the 'Both findings can stand' architectural-fork template; the verdict file already names this alternative. I prefer documented_incommensurability because the record does pose a numeric gap (0.20 AUC) whose uncertainty does not overlap (P-1232's interval excludes 0.901; recomputed Hanley-McNeil for 0.901 with 24 v 24 gives about 0.810-0.992, excluding 0.700), so the disagreement does not dissolve into agreement; it cannot be adjudicated precisely because the quantities differ, which is what outcome 2 records. Either label excludes genuine and the substance is identical.
C-237.grounds_check: All seven grounds are supported by the papers. Ground 1 (different predictors): P-1232 p5 names the three-lncRNA combination; P-1254 p2 names the four preselected miRNAs and p1/p7 the single-marker ROCs. Ground 2 (no crossing ordering claim): P-1232 p5 'more credible' compares the panel to its own single lncRNAs; the p8 lncRNA-versus-miRNA remark follows 'It has been established that lncRNAs possess a broader range of biological functions compared to miRNAs' and is about scope; P-1254 has no lncRNA mention at all. Ground 3 (population differs): confirmed from P-1232 p2 (MMSE <=17/<=20/<=24 by education) and Table 1, and P-1254 p2 (MoCA < 26) and Table 3 (age 73.35 v 78.12; MoCA 26.17 v 20.37). Ground 5 (incompatible if same): P-1232's CI excludes 0.901; my Hanley-McNeil recomputation (SE about 0.0465) matches the file's 0.81-0.99. Ground 6 (record overstates P-1232 validation): p3 'blood RNA profiles from ... AddNeuroMed', p4 'We selected two genes (ATP2A2 and PSEN1)', p5 'validated the predictive power of target genes', p9 'we only evaluated the predictive effect of target exo-lncRNAs in the Chinese population'. Ground 7 (flag does not apply to P-1254): highest AUC 0.901, implied accuracy 43/48 = 0.896; 100% specificity is neither accuracy nor AUC under the Section 2 test. Ground 4 (dataset-family gate fails, no waiver) is consistent with the record's own dataset_equal: false and with the C-232 precedent (ADNI v NACC treated as a mismatch), but it is the least load-bearing ground: applied strictly it fails every own-cohort pair, and the file itself says a waiver would not change the outcome. One small internal tension: the gates entry says validation tier 'match in substance' (both AUCs in-sample), yet record_defect 3 adds 'the registry validation tiers also differ (V3 vs V2)' as if that contradicted the record's 'all four gates pass'. In substance the record's validation_tier_comparable: true is correct; the V3/V2 discrepancy is a registry-row error (rightly listed as defect 6), not evidence against the record's gate claim. Only the dataset gate contradicts 'all four pass'. No ground is wrong; this one clause is a slight overstatement.
C-237.quote_check: All 16 evidence quotes were located by grep at the stated pages (page boundaries checked against the '=== page N ===' markers). The three the verdict most depends on: (1) P-1232 p5, extract lines 609-612: 'the AUC of ROC curves for the combination of plasma exosomal LINC001380, ENST00000484033 and ENST00000531087 was 70.0 % (CI: 64.1 %-76.0 %, P < 0.001) with a sensitivity of 72.0 % and a specificity of 60.7 % (Fig. 4A).' (2) P-1254 p1, lines 32-35: 'we evaluated miR-483-5p (Area Under the Curve (AUC) is 0.901, sensitivity 79.2 % and specificity 100 %) and miR-502-5p (AUC is 0.872, sensitivity 79.2 % and specificity 83.3 %)'. (3) P-1254 p7 Fig 4e legend, lines 578-579: 'Receiver operating characteristic curves for miR-483-5p and miR-502-5p to discriminate MCI from age-matched control.' which fixes the ROC at 24 v 24 (sens 79.2% = 19/24 corroborates 24 cases). For the principal record defect, P-1232 p9 lines 871-874: 'although we used dataset from the UK population to validate the predictive effect of target genes on MCI, we only evaluated the predictive effect of target exo-lncRNAs in the Chinese population.' Also confirmed: p2 '1:1 proportion-matched 155 non-MCI' (lines 162-164), p2 'education-specific cut-off point' (192-193), Table 1 MMSE row (315-319), p3 AddNeuroMed (292), p4 two genes (409), p5 external validation of target genes (616-617), p8 'broader research space' (768-771); P-1254 p2 preselected candidates (117-119), MoCA < 26 (149-150), 24 and 24 chosen at random (156-157), Table 3 age (449-453) and MoCA (458-462) rows. The Elsevier extract renders the en-dash and inequality signs cleanly here; no decoding was needed for any load-bearing number.
C-237.defects_check: The record_defects list is correct against the papers, with one clause slightly overreaching and one item minor. Defect 1 (record's 'WITH external validation' / 'externally validated, AUC 0.700') is the most consequential and is fully contradicted by P-1232 p3, p4, p5 and p9: the external GSE63060 analysis used blood RNA profiles for ATP2A2 and PSEN1, and 0.700 is the in-sample panel figure. Defect 2 ('n=72 ROC cohort', '0.901 ... on n=72') is correct: the ROC is MCI v age-matched controls, 24 v 24 = 48 (Fig 4e legend; 19/24 = 79.2%); the 24 under-65 controls are outside it. Defect 3 ('all four deterministic gates pass') is correct on the dataset gate, which the record's own dataset_equal: false contradicts; the appended 'registry validation tiers also differ (V3 vs V2)' overreaches slightly, because the file's own gates entry treats validation tier as matched in substance, so the V3/V2 gap is a registry error rather than a failed gate. Defect 4 ('cross-sectional community cohorts') is valid but minor: P-1232 self-describes as a 1:1 matched case-control study recruited from the community; neither is a cohort study, though 'cohort' is used loosely as 'sample' throughout the ledger. Defect 5 ('n=310 discovery') is valid: 310 is total enrolment, the AUC comes from 150 v 150, and RNA-seq used a small subset; the Methods 'five ... cases and their corresponding control' versus Results 'randomly selected 10 MCI patients and corresponding healthy controls from 310 samples, and another 300 samples for qRT-PCR' tension is real in the text, but the 310 - 300 arithmetic implies ten sequenced samples in total, so the challenger's softening (reconcilable with five pairs) is the better reading. Defect 6 (registry row: V3 overstates the panel's validation; Sample_N_Approx 'miRNA/ROC cohort 72' should distinguish the 72-person miRNA cohort from the 48-person ROC) is fair. No defect is missing from the ledger record itself. The challenger's added observation that P-1254's control MoCA SD of 1.14 around mean 26.17 is impossible for 24 integer scores all >= 26 (I recomputed the maximum as about 0.82) is a paper-internal inconsistency, not a ledger defect, so its absence from record_defects is correct; it would belong in a note on P-1254's block if the adjudicator wants it recorded.
C-237.would_change: A corpus study measuring the three lncRNAs and miR-483-5p in one cohort under one case definition, or either marker set re-measured in the other's population, with uncertainty excluding the other's estimate; no such study exists (marker names occur only in the P-1232 and P-1254 blocks). Nothing short of a paper claiming, on measured accuracy, that exosomal lncRNA panels outperform or underperform exosomal single miRNAs would move this toward genuine; P-1232's p8 remark is about biological scope and P-1254 never mentions lncRNAs. If the adjudicator decides that every record written on the 'Both findings can stand' fork template is to be closed under outcome 1(c) regardless of a surviving numeric gap, the label moves to false_positive with identical substance and grounds; the verdict file already states this alternative.

C-258.verdict_assessment: false_positive stands under the rule as written and as applied across round 18. Both PDFs are the right papers and both were read in full. The two results point the same way and both are significant: P-680 aerobic SMD 1.442 (0.642-2.260 in Results 3.4; 0.624-2.260 in Abstract and Discussion) and all-exercise 1.165 (0.741-1.589); P-683 aerobic-without-music g 0.48 (0.18-0.79), 0.6 (0.28-0.93) with high-RoB trials removed, multivariate global cognition 0.53 (0.16-0.90). The intervals overlap (0.642-0.79 aerobic; 0.741-0.79 all-exercise), and the brief's gloss reads same-direction results with overlapping intervals as compatible, which is outcome 1 in the order. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes: P-680 runs no between-type test and P-683's PICOS excludes resistance and multimodal exercise. Genuine is excluded on any reading because the quantities are not the same: P-680 pools one composite of all cognitive tests per study (its own Limitations, p.15), P-683 pools the global-cognition screening domain only (MMSE, ADAS-Cog, MoCA, NCSE, NTB; Appendix C); P-680's 'aerobic' stratum is Amjad, Bademli, Qi, Song & Yu, Varela (2 arms), of which P-683 classes Song & Yu as aerobic WITH music (background music, Appendix G), Qi 2018 (same DOI 10.3892/etm.2018.7006) as dance, and excludes Bademli for lack of music information (Appendix F), so only Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012 sit in both contested strata; P-680 drops its four amnestic-labelled trials while P-683's AEwtM node includes Tarumi 2019, Stuckenschneider 2021 and Yogev-Seligmann 2021, all amnestic. Not partially_resolved (no real disagreement on a comparable quantity, no third studies) and not unresolved. The one caveat for the adjudicator: this is the thinnest FP in the round. Unlike C-255, where each point estimate lies inside the other's interval, here each point estimate lies OUTSIDE the other's interval (0.48 below 0.642; 1.442 above 0.79) and the overlap is a 0.15-wide sliver between a 1.6-wide and a 0.6-wide interval; I re-derived the verdict's difference test at z about 2.2 (aerobic) and 2.6 (all-exercise). The brief's incompatibility definition contains both 'reported uncertainty excludes the other' and 'NOT incompatible ... with overlapping intervals', and the round has consistently resolved that tension via the overlap clause. If the adjudicator instead reads the exclusion clause first, the label becomes documented_incommensurability (as C-257 and C-264 also note), never genuine.
C-258.grounds_check: All four grounds are supported by the papers; two have minor blemishes. Ground 1 (direction and overlap): correct, every figure verified. Ground 2 (no ordering refuted): correct in substance, but its final clause 'P-683's music contrast has no counterpart in P-680 [q9]' cites the wrong anchor; q9 is P-680's metric sentence ('pre-post correlation and standardized by score sd changes', p.3) and says nothing about music. The fact stands on Table 2 (p.7), where Song & Yu 2019 appears as plain 'Aerobic Exercise (Stepping Exercise Program)' and P-680 mentions music nowhere. Ground 3 (different quantities): fully supported by q6, q7, q12, q13, q16, q17, Appendix G and Table 2. Ground 4 (blood-marker criterion not applied as a requirement): correct and important, but slightly under-counted. The verdict repeats the paper's own tallies ('three' in the Discussion p.14, 'four' in the Limitations p.15); Table 2 actually shows blood markers for five included studies (Nascimento, Chupel, Damirchi, Sungkarat 2018, Molina-Sotomayor) with NR for the other eighteen. Either way the record's 'biomarker-reporting subset' explanation collapses. Gates: task T6/T6, dataset family (both pool published MCI exercise trials), validation n/a, modality family match at family level are all right; the six shared trials (Varela, Amjad, Song & Yu, Qi, Tarumi/Thomas, Stuckenschneider) are correctly recorded under independence and I confirmed each in both rosters. Independence statements (different teams Coimbra/Macquarie; P-683 does not cite Akalp; P-683 pool from Quan et al. 2024 plus database search) all verified.
C-258.quote_check: I confirmed the load-bearing quotes verbatim in the extracts, not only by the machine check: q1 (P-680 p.1, lines 38-40, abstract with 0.624), q2 (P-680 p.5, 'varied from 0.642 to 2.260'), q10 (P-683 p.6, 'AEwtM demonstrated a low-to-moderate effect (k = 26, g = 0.48 [0.18, 0.79])'), q6 (P-680 p.15, composite cognitive scores combining all domains), q7 (P-680 p.14, the five aerobic trials), q12/q13/q17 (P-683 p.5, the AEwM, dance and AEwtM rosters), q3/q4 (P-680 p.5 amnestic exclusion), q16 (P-683 p.18 Bademli exclusion), q14/q15 (matching DOI in both reference lists), q21-q23 (Table 2 rows). Also verified but not quoted in the file: P-683 Appendix G entries for Song & Yu ('music was used as background stimulus'), Varela ('performed without music'), Qi 2018 (dance) and Amjad (AEwtM); Appendix L 0.6 [0.28, 0.93]; Appendix E 0.53 [0.16, 0.9] at rho 0.6; Appendix O AEwM vs AEwtM 0.73 [-0.09, 1.56] with no direct evidence; P-683 Table 2 N = 11 trials, n = 683 for AEwtM global cognition, with no list of which 11. No quote is misattributed or altered. The only citation problem is the q9 anchor noted under grounds.
C-258.defects_check: All six record_defects are correct against the PDFs. (1) The blood-marker requirement: the criterion text exists (p.3) but Table 2 shows NR for most studies and the paper itself counts 3 or 4 marker studies; the record's leading causal story has no basis. (2) The P-683 'cross-check suggesting the latter is inflated' quote is fabricated: P-683 never cites Akalp et al. 2024 and no such sentence exists. (3) 'Same outcome domain (global cognition)' is wrong for P-680's estimand; the record's error is understandable because P-680 itself uses 'global cognitive function' loosely (Methods p.3, sections 3.3 and 3.6) to mean its all-domain composite, which the verdict could have said. (4) 'Only like-for-like pair' is wrong; the strata share only Amjad and Varela. The bundled 'same intervention family' is a slight overstatement of a defect, since at the coarse aerobic-family level the phrase is defensible and the verdict's own gates section says 'match at the family level'. (5) Both rosters are printed (P-680 Table 2, P-683 Appendix G) and the record's own residual_risk asked for exactly this roster diff; six shared trials settle it. (6) The 0.642/0.624 inconsistency is real and immaterial. Two things the verdict did not list but the adjudicator should know: the record's verification block claims 'All 14 quotes verified verbatim', yet beyond the fabricated one several record 'quotes' are paraphrases (e.g. the amnestic-exclusion sentence, the I-squared/no-meta-regression sentence, the P-683 methods sentence), accurate in substance but not verbatim, so that verification claim is itself unreliable; and P-680 is internally inconsistent on its own counts (4 amnestic + 18 non-amnestic stated on p.5 versus 4 + 19 in Table 2; 3 versus 4 versus 5 blood-marker studies), none of which bears on the verdict.
C-258.would_change: The label would move to documented_incommensurability, not genuine, if the adjudicator either (a) applies the quantity test before the compatibility test, as in the C-234 reclassification, or (b) declines to treat a 0.642-0.79 sliver of overlap between intervals whose point estimates each lie outside the other's interval as 'compatible' (difference test z about 2.2 aerobic, 2.6 all-exercise, treating them as independent estimates of one parameter, which they are not). Nothing in either PDF can move it to genuine: P-680 reports no estimate on P-683's estimand (global-cognition domain, aerobic exercise without music, amnestic trials included) and P-683 reports none on P-680's (all-domain composite, aerobic including dance and music-accompanied stepping, amnestic trials excluded); the only trials the two contested strata share are Amjad 2019 and Varela 2012. Small corrections to the verdict file before acceptance: re-anchor ground 2's music clause to Table 2 rather than q9; count blood-marker studies from Table 2 (five) alongside the paper's 3/4; soften 'same intervention family' to 'same stratum composition'.

C-266.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category under the brief's ordering. Both source documents were read in full (P-1407 = Donaghy et al., Mov Disord 2025, DOI 10.1002/mds.30181; P-1267 = Schraen-Maschke et al., Neurobiol Dis 2024, 106459; both pack files are the right papers). P-1407 Table 1 (p.3) prints Abeta42/40 hazard ratios in all three groups with the ratio inverted so that a higher value means more abnormal (p.2 Methods; footnote a): all MCI 1.06 (0.83-1.35) p=0.636, probable MCI-LB 1.23 (0.94-1.60) p=0.130, MCI-AD 0.67 (0.37-1.20) p=0.180. P-1267 reports per-point adjusted HRs of 0.95 (0.91-0.99) free and 0.92 (0.86-0.98) total, and top-quartile-vs-rest HRs of 0.36 (0.15-0.87) and 0.37 (0.16-0.89). Two of P-1407's three estimates therefore point the same way as P-1267 (lower ratio, higher hazard) and differ only in significance, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict. The one opposite point estimate (MCI-AD 0.67) is unsupported by P-1407's own statistics (interval spans 1), so the 'opposite directions each supported' limb fails. I independently reproduced the challenger's rescaling: P-1267's per-SD-more-abnormal HR is 1.454 (1.076-1.991) free and 1.455 (1.095-1.971) total, which overlaps P-1407's MCI-AD 0.37-1.20 unless one Newcastle control SD on the Simoa scale equals more than 2.0-2.5 BALTAZAR MCI-sample SDs; neither paper supports that and controls are normally less variable than MCI, so the plausible direction of error increases the overlap. No reported interval excludes the other. The record also misreads P-1407 (see defects), which is a second independent limb of false_positive. Genuine is not available: no statistically supported opposite direction, and the dataset-family gate fails without waiver. documented_incommensurability is the only serious alternative (dementia-or-death vs dementia censored at 36 months; Lewy-body-enriched vs Lewy-body-excluded MCI; per-control-SD Simoa vs per-point/top-quartile INNO-BIA), but the brief applies false_positive first and both of its limbs are met, so the verdict's placement is correct and its flag of the estimand-first alternative is honest. Note for the adjudicator: first reader, challenger and this reader are all Claude models, so this is a third reading against the source text, not an independent-model check.
C-266.grounds_check: Grounds 1, 2, 4 and 6 are supported by the papers as quoted. Three overstatements, none load-bearing: (a) Ground 3, second sentence: 'The authors attribute their MCI-AD nulls to 43 cases and 21 events' overgeneralises. P-1407 p.4 gives that explanation only for 'The absence of an association of pTau181 and disease progression', not for Abeta42/40 or for the MCI-AD nulls collectively; the paper offers no explanation for the Abeta42/40 null. The first sentence of Ground 3 (0.67 unsupported by the study's own statistics) stands on its own. (b) Ground 5 is overstated in two ways: 'grouping the lower quartiles after inspection' ignores that the Methods (p.5) pre-announce the highest-quartile-versus-three-lower analysis, citing the gradient seen in Hanon et al. 2022 in the same cohort (the Results p.6 add an observed-pattern justification, so the wording is partly fair but incomplete); and 'conditional on adjustment' holds for the free ratio only, since the total ratio's top-quartile contrast is significant unadjusted (0.36, 0.15-0.85, p=0.019) and the total continuous HR is borderline (0.94, p=0.053). This ground is context about P-1267's fragility and does not bear on whether the pair conflicts. (c) Ground 4's 'precision, not direction' is exact for the whole-cohort and MCI-LB estimates; for MCI-AD the point-estimate direction does differ, though unsupported. The ground's core claim, that no reported interval excludes the other because the printed figures cannot be put on a common scale (P-1407 prints no control SD), is correct. Ground 6(d), the dataset-family mismatch, is factually correct as stated; the challenger rightly notes a cross-cohort waiver has precedent (C-232), but (a)-(c) carry the hypothetical without it. Minor inferences in what_each_reports/quantity_a already flagged by the challenger are confirmed: P-1407 never says its Simoa values are a 'total' fraction; P-1267 reports the one death (p.5) without saying how it was handled.
C-266.quote_check: Independently confirmed by grep on the regenerated pack files, with line positions: P-1407 Table 1 rows 'MCI-AD (n = 43) / Aβ42/40 / a / 0.67 (0.37–1.20) / 0.180' (lines 340-344), 'All MCI (n = 120) ... 1.06 (0.83–1.35) / 0.636' (312-316), 'Probable MCI-LB (n = 62) ... 1.23 (0.94–1.60) / 0.130' (326-330); 'The Aβ42/40 ratio was inversed and so a greater value represents greater abnormality to allow for direct comparison of hazard ratios.' (193-195); 'hazard ratios for conversion to dementia or death with correction for age, sex, years in education, and MMSE.' (187-189); 'MMSE and blood results were standardized with respect to the control mean.' (190-191); 'In the entire MCI cohort, 72/131 participants (55%) converted to dementia or died.' (233-234); footnote 'aResults have been reversed to allow for direct comparison of hazard ratios.' (363). P-1267: 'HR = 0.36 (0.15–0.87), p = 0.022, for the free ratio' (898); Table 3 free-ratio row '0.97 (0.93–1.02) / 0.21 / 0.95 (0.91–0.99) / 0.038' (933-936) with column order confirmed as unadjusted (+) then adjusted (*) from the header (906-909) and footnotes (1007-1008); '0.92 (0.86–0.98) / 0.013' (940-941); 'censored at M36 as only one patient converted to AD later' (254); '47.2% (n = 50) of the MCI participants converted to dementia and among them, 96% (n = 48) to probable AD.' (626-628); 'To increase the likelihood of conversion to AD, we excluded participants with Lewy Body, Parkinsonian, frontotemporal, or vascular MCI disorders.' (1329-1331). The dichotomised block (994-1005) is scrambled by extraction; the adjusted pairing (0.36 free, 0.37 total) is confirmed by the text on p.6 and the '64 and 63%' on p.9, and the unadjusted assignment (0.43 free, 0.36 total) follows the free-then-total order of the row labels at 988-993. The three quotes the verdict most depends on (the MCI-AD 0.67 row, the inversion sentence, and P-1267's 0.95/0.36 figures) all match verbatim.
C-266.defects_check: All four record_defects are correct against the papers. (1) The conflict_statement's '72 conversions' misdescribes composite dementia-or-death events (p.3: 'converted to dementia or died'), and the Abeta42/40 Cox models use n=120/62/43, not 131 (Table 1). Correct; the '~2.7 years' is one of the two follow-up figures the paper itself gives (3 years p.2, 2.7 years p.3) and is rightly not flagged. (2) 'No prognostic value ... in any group' recasts three non-significant HRs, two in P-1267's direction, as evidence of absence. Correct. (3) The review_note and the 2026-09-14 blocker flag say there is no HR, CI or p-value for Abeta42/40 and 'no HR from P-1407 that could be placed against P-1267's HR 0.36'; Table 1 prints all three. Correct. One nuance the verdict could have added: the review_note's wording was 'in the block', so the original observation about the summary block may have been true, and the defect is that the blocker flag then turned a block omission into a claim about the paper. (4) '62 probable MCI-LB of 131 with outcome data' conflates the Cox-model n (62) with the event denominator (63) and uses a phrase the paper does not; enrichment itself correct. Correct. No missed defect of substance: claim_b and the P-1267 numbers in the conflict_statement match the paper; 'roughly 60% lower' matches the paper's 'at least 60%'. One could add that conflict_type 'semantic_directional' mislabels a pair in which two of three P-1407 estimates share P-1267's direction, but that is a label rather than a factual claim and is covered by defect (2). The pack_defects (wrong first-pack PDFs; registry task_substage 'MCI_to_AD' and population_specificity 'general' for a half-Lewy-body cohort with a dementia-or-death endpoint) are also accurate on the evidence read.
C-266.would_change: Genuine would require a statistically supported opposite direction on a comparable estimand: for example, a Lewy-body-excluded MCI cohort showing that a higher Abeta42/40 ratio carries a significantly higher hazard of dementia on a per-point or per-SD contrast, plus a dataset-family waiver on record. Neither paper contains such a result. The compatibility conclusion would only fail if P-1407's unprinted control SD on the Simoa scale were more than about 2.0-2.5 BALTAZAR MCI-sample SDs AND the adjudicator accepted a cross-platform rescaling as 'reported uncertainty'; both are implausible and the rule speaks of reported intervals. If the adjudicator's house convention is to classify by estimand before compatibility (as in the C-234 reclassification), the same facts give documented_incommensurability, which the verdict already names; that would change the label, not the conclusion that the pair is not genuine.

C-267.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category. On the contested quantity (pooled CSF YKL-40, AD minus MCI) both meta-analyses place AD above MCI: P-1427 SMD 0.25 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.57, p = 0.134, 15 studies, I2 89.2%), described by its authors as 'an increasing trend'; P-1337 random-effects z = 2.02, p = 0.0429, 7 studies, I2 97.4%. That is a significance-only difference in the same direction, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict, and the brief's ordering applies false_positive before incommensurability when results are compatible. P-1427 itself frames the difference as an update of P-1337 (its ref 7): 'Other meta-analyses, often based on a limited number of studies, reported higher CSF YKL-40 levels in AD than in MCI ... By synthesizing more recent evidence, our updated analysis suggests ...' (pp.8-9). No reading yields genuine: neither paper reports MCI above AD, P-1337's z = 2.02 puts its lower bound near zero (about 3% of its point estimate), and its pooled metric is evidently unstandardised (tau2 values of 170 to 1970 are impossible for an SMD; figure captions say 'weighted mean differences ... pg/mL'), so magnitudes cannot be set against P-1427's SMD anyway. The one live alternative is documented_incommensurability on the same facts (SMD vs apparent MD; any-MCI vs 'MCI'/stable MCI comparator), and the operator's own C-234 reclassification of 2026-09-24 took exactly that route (different quantities first, compatible results as the second ground). The verdict file discloses this fork honestly. Under the round-18 brief's explicit ordering I uphold false_positive; if the adjudicator wants round-18 verdicts aligned with the C-234 precedent, documented_incommensurability is the consistent relabel and changes nothing about the review's count of genuine contradictions.

C-265.verdict_assessment: documented_incommensurability is the right category and should stand. The two papers give divergent headline answers to a similarly worded question (P-1403 title: plasma p-tau217 identifies CU adults who will develop cognitive impairment; P-1421 abstract: no biomarker was associated with MCI development from normal cognition), so this is not a false_positive. But no estimate in either paper is on a quantity the other reports. P-1403's only hazard ratios are by joint plasma A/T group against A-T- (Methods p.4: 'Cox proportional hazard models were used to assess the risk of MCI progression by AT group'), with T+ set 2 SD above the Abeta-PET-negative mean (13% of the sample, 97% specificity, 34% sensitivity for progression, p.8); its continuous result is ROC AUC, not a hazard ratio. P-1421's p-tau217 hazard ratio is a single-marker high/low split at a Youden cut-off tuned to 10-year all-cause dementia (37% of the sample 'high') or a spline against the cohort median, from a Gompertz multistate model on an age time scale that allows MCI reversion. The rule names predictor set/input representation, endpoint construct and population behind the shared label as differences that make results unsettable against each other, and all three apply: exposure (joint A/T at an AD-anchored threshold vs single marker at a dementia-optimised threshold), MCI construct (blinded consensus requiring complaint and/or observed decline over annual visits vs a per-visit 1.5 SD single-domain psychometric state assessed every 3 or 6 years with reversion modelled) and population (family-history-enriched, mean age 65 at classification, vs random community sample, median 72, 40% aged 78+, 62.5% of whom have chronic kidney disease per Table 1, and P-1421 itself notes biomarker levels rise with age in unimpaired people, p.5). The dataset-family gate also fails without a waiver, which under the brief is itself sufficient for this category, but the verdict correctly does not rest on it: as in C-232, a cohort waiver would not cure the predictor mismatch. I considered genuine on the challenger's strongest case (P-1403's effect sits on the tau dimension, A+T- is null, and the authors say Abeta did not add to tau, so the A+T+ contrast is in substance a p-tau217 contrast; P-1421's spline null spans its whole range). It fails because a high/low hazard ratio depends on where the cut falls (13% vs 37% positive), no method on record places P-1403's 3.98 pg/mL in-house plasma threshold on P-1421's ALZpath serum z-axis, and the nearest true tau-only pairing (A-T+ vs A-T-, 7 vs 127 participants, HR 4.25, 1.60-11.31) overlaps P-1421's fully adjusted interval (0.75-1.88). partially_resolved_candidate does not fit: the only explanations available are 'different quantities' explanations, which the brief routes to incommensurability, and no third corpus study bridges the pair. unresolved does not fit: the documents settle that the estimands differ.
C-265.grounds_check: All seven grounds are supported by the papers; two are slightly overstated as standalone grounds and one defect-facing claim is a little strong. Ground 1 (exposure contrasts differ): fully supported; A+T+ 21/215 = 10% (p.4), 803/2148 high in P-1421 (Table 2), no A/T classification anywhere in P-1421, P-1403 Cox models by AT group only and continuous analysis as ROC AUC (p.4, p.8). Ground 2 (population behind the label): supported; first-degree family history (p.3), SNAC-K random sample 60+ with median 72.2 and 865/2148 aged 78+ (Table 1), the p.10 and p.5 quotes are accurate, and P-1403 names community settings as untested (p.3). Ground 3 (dataset gate fails, C-232 reasoning): supported; the record carries no waiver, and the C-232 reclassification grounds read 'the mismatch was not waived and confounds the cohort difference that was waived', which is exactly what the ground says. Ground 4 (endpoint and horizon): the endpoint-construct half is solid (p.4 vs p.6-7). The 'horizon' half is weak as a standalone reason, since a hazard ratio under proportional hazards is not a horizon-specific quantity the way a t-year cumulative incidence is; the substantive difference is the model (Cox on time since sampling with annual visits vs Gompertz multistate on an age scale with 3- or 6-year interval censoring and reversion), which the verdict states in quantity_b but not in the ground itself. Ground 5 (matrix and assay): supported but overstated if read alone, because P-1421 itself says serum levels 'correlate closely with plasma levels and show comparable diagnostic performance' (p.6, refs 44-46); the assay/threshold difference carries the weight, not serum vs plasma. Ground 6 (amyloid arm null in both): supported (p.7; Table 2). Ground 7 (fairness: continuous null holds, headline answers diverge, no like-for-like HR): supported by p.2 text. The gates.task note that P-1421's registry substage MCI_to_AD describes only its headline result while the paper also reports NC to MCI is correct and important: an automated substage gate would have blocked this pair, so the substantive reading is right.

P-1421's point estimates are 1.07 and 1.19, above 1, so the pair is a strong positive association against a null in the same nominal direction, not opposite directions. Nothing material was missed. Two record-quality observations outside the defect list, for the adjudicator rather than the ledger: the record's evidence_quotes are the claim strings themselves (verbatim from summary blocks, as the review_note admits), not passages from the papers; and the P-1421 registry row codes task_substage MCI_to_AD and prediction_horizon 'not reported' although the paper reports the NC-to-MCI transition and follow-up up to 16 years, which is why a deterministic substage gate would not have surfaced this pair.
C-265.would_change: The verdict file's own conditions are right and I would keep them: a dataset-family waiver stated on the record together with a like-for-like exposure from either side (SNAC-K reporting an NC-to-MCI hazard ratio for an A/T classification or for an AD-pathology-anchored p-tau217 threshold, or PREVENT-AD reporting a whole-sample single-marker p-tau217 hazard ratio or spline), still giving non-overlapping intervals. Two further things would move me: an age-restricted SNAC-K NC-to-MCI estimate for participants under 78 (closer to PREVENT-AD's age 65), since Table 1 shows the 78+ stratum drives the upper p-tau217 quantiles and carries 62.5% chronic kidney disease, which would test whether the population ground is doing real work; and an accepted method on record for matching thresholds across assays by percentile, under which P-1421's Figure 1 spline could be read at the z-score corresponding to P-1403's top-13% cut. If that reading showed a flat curve with an upper bound well below 4 at that point, the challenger's 'no threshold at which HR 4 to 8 could appear' argument would gain force and the pair would move toward genuine on the tau arm. Neither is available in the source text: the extract gives only axis labels for Figure 1, and the brief does not admit cross-assay percentile matching. Also, if the MCI constructs were shown to be interchangeable (P-1421's CIND sensitivity analysis is said to be 'comparable', p.2, but the CIND and consensus definitions still differ on the complaint/decline requirement and reversion), the endpoint ground would weaken.

C-264.verdict_assessment: false_positive is the right category. P-1341's blood NfL estimates (plasma SMD 0.10, 95% CI -0.36 to 0.56, P=.67, p.3; Simoa = all three blood comparisons, SMD 0.01, -0.38 to 0.41, P=.95, p.4) are non-significant nulls with wide intervals; P-1231's aMCI-vs-control blood NfL ratio of means is 1.24 (1.17-1.32, p<0.001, p.3). Neither interval excludes the other: converting P-1231's 17-32% elevation onto P-1341's own Table 1 dispersions gives implied SMDs of 0.24-0.83 across the three blood studies (I reproduced the verdict's figures exactly), all inside P-1341's plasma interval. Under the rule this is a significant-vs-non-significant difference with overlapping intervals, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict. P-1341 asserts no equivalence; it hedges ('may be not a biomarker', 'more studies on blood NfL are needed', p.5) and names small samples as its first limitation. A 3-comparison null (Lin n=83, Steinacker n=17, Thijssen n=47 cases) against a 23-study positive is absence of evidence, not contradiction. I considered documented_incommensurability (SMD vs RoM; MCI-any vs aMCI; 3 vs 23 studies) and genuine (the two papers' CONCLUSIONS about blood NfL do read as opposed). Neither fits better: the brief applies false_positive first when the results are compatible, and they are; and the rule binds 'incompatible' to results, not to conclusion wording. The verdict category should stand.
C-264.grounds_check: Ground 1 (same direction): supported by the numbers but slightly overstated. The pooled point estimates 0.10 and 0.01 are above zero, but they are essentially null; at study level two of P-1341's three blood studies point negative (Table 1: Steinacker 16.6 vs 21.7, own SMD about -0.33; Thijssen 14 vs 15.2, about -0.15; only Lin 20 vs 17.8 is positive, about +0.32). The accurate statement is 'null estimates whose intervals contain P-1231's effect', which is what the rule needs; the verdict does not turn on the direction wording. Ground 2 (significance only; P-1341 hedges): supported, p.5 quotes verbatim. Ground 3 (intervals do not exclude each other): supported; I recomputed the conversion from Table 1 and got 0.44-0.83 (Lin), 0.24-0.44 (Steinacker), 0.32-0.61 (Thijssen), matching the verdict to two decimals; the plasma interval -0.36 to 0.56 overlaps all three, the Simoa interval -0.38 to 0.41 overlaps two (not Lin). Appropriately labelled as the adjudicator's own approximation. Ground 4 (record misreads P-1341; ELISA=CSF, Simoa=blood): fully supported by Table 1 (p.3): Wallin, Hampel, Olsson, Lleo are all ELISA/CSF; Lin, Steinacker, Thijssen are all Simoa/blood; the ELISA estimate (0.61, 0.21-1.01) is identical to the CSF estimate. Ground 5 (would be incommensurable anyway): metric and case-label differences are correctly sourced (P-1231 p.2). The assay claim 'Simoa only vs pooled platforms (P-1231 p.6)' is a little overstated: p.6 is the Fig. 5 caption covering all blood biomarkers, and the text never says which platforms the 23 NfL studies used; since blood NfL is in practice almost always Simoa (P-1341 p.4 says ELISA is 'mainly restricted to CSF'), the assay mix may not differ much. Immaterial to a false_positive verdict.

C-264.would_change: A P-1341 blood estimate whose interval excluded the P-1231-implied effect (upper bound below about 0.24 SMD on these dispersions) or a significantly negative blood SMD; neither exists.
